## ⚠️ Command Breakdown

## ⚠️ Security Warning

Disabling SELinux is **strongly discouraged** in production environments because:
| Risk | Detail |
|------|--------|
| 🔓 Removes mandatory access control | Processes run with fewer restrictions |
| 🦠 Increases attack surface | Exploits can move laterally more easily |
| 📋 Compliance violations | May violate PCI-DSS, HIPAA, etc. |

---

## ✅ Safer Alternatives

```bash
# Option 1: Permissive mode only (logs but doesn't block)
setenforce 0
sed -i 's/SELINUX=enforcing/SELINUX=permissive/' /etc/selinux/config

# Option 2: Fix a specific SELinux denial instead
ausearch -m avc -ts recent | audit2allow -M mypolicy
semodule -i mypolicy.pp
```
